'''Boris Vladimirovich Svistunov''' ({{langx|ru|Борис Владимирович Свистунов}}; born October 22, 1959) is a Russian-American physicist specialised in the [[condensed matter physics]]. He received his [[MSc]] in physics in 1983 from Moscow Engineering Physics Institute, Moscow. In 1990, he received his [[PhD]] in theoretical physics from Kurchatov Institute (Moscow), where he worked from 1986 to 2003 (and is still affiliated with). In 2003, he joined the Physics Department of the University of Massachusetts, Amherst where he is currently full professor. He is currently also an affiliated faculty member of Wilczek Quantum Center in<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://wqc.physics.sjtu.edu.cn/|title=Home|website=wqc.physics.sjtu.edu.cn|access-date=September 30, 2018}}</ref> [[Shanghai]] at SJTU and is a participant of Simons collaboration on many electron systems.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.simonsfoundation.org/team/boris-svistunov/|title=Boris Svistunov {{!}} Simons Foundation|website=simonsfoundation.org|language=en-US|access-date=September 30, 2018|date=February 19, 2014}}</ref>

Boris Svistunov is recognised for his works on superfluidity, supersolidity, superfluid turbulence, strongly correlated systems and pioneering numerical approaches. With his collaborators and students he made important contributions to superfluid turbulence<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Kozik|first1=E. V.|last2=Svistunov|first2=B. V.|date=July 28, 2009|title=Theory of Decay of Superfluid Turbulence in the Low-Temperature Limit|journal=Journal of Low Temperature Physics|language=en|volume=156|issue=3–6|pages=215–267|doi=10.1007/s10909-009-9914-y|issn=0022-2291|arxiv=0904.1379|bibcode=2009JLTP..156..215K|s2cid=16786112}}</ref> (reviewed in<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|url=https://www.crcpress.com/Superfluid-States-of-Matter/Svistunov-Babaev-Prokofev/p/book/9781439802755|title=Superfluid States of Matter|date=April 15, 2015|website=CRC Press|language=en|access-date=October 2, 2018}}</ref>), theory of supersolids, in collaboration with [[Nikolay Prokof'ev]] including the theory of superfluidity of crystalline defects<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Prokof'ev|first1=Nikolay|last2=Svistunov|first2=Boris|date=April 20, 2005|title=Supersolid State of Matter|journal=Physical Review Letters|volume=94|issue=15|article-number=155302|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.94.155302|pmid=15904155|arxiv=cond-mat/0409472|bibcode=2005PhRvL..94o5302P|s2cid=45498667}}</ref> (reviewed in<ref name=":0" />) and [[superglass]] phase.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Boninsegni|first1=Massimo|last2=Prokof'ev|first2=Nikolay|last3=Svistunov|first3=Boris|date=March 16, 2006|title=Superglass Phase of $^{4}\mathrm{He}$|journal=Physical Review Letters|volume=96|issue=10|article-number=105301|doi=10.1103/PhysRevLett.96.105301|pmid=16605751|arxiv=cond-mat/0512103}}</ref>

He is a co-inventor, with Nikolay Prokof'ev and Igor Tupitsyn of the widely used Worm Monte-Carlo algorithm. With Nikolay Prokof'ev he invented Diagrammatic Monte-Carlo method<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://wiki.phys.ethz.ch/quantumsimulations/_media/svistunov1_1.pdf|title=slides}}</ref> which is stochastic summation of Feynman diagrammatic series. Because the method is free from the [[Numerical sign problem]]<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Rossi|first1=R.|last2=Prokof'ev|first2=N.|last3=Svistunov|first3=B.|last4=Van Houcke|first4=K.|last5=Werner|first5=F.|date=April 1, 2017|title=Polynomial complexity despite the fermionic sign|journal=EPL (Europhysics Letters)|volume=118|issue=1|article-number=10004|doi=10.1209/0295-5075/118/10004|issn=0295-5075|arxiv=1703.10141|bibcode=2017EL....11810004R|s2cid=17929942}}</ref> it allowed to solve previously untreatable fermionic problems.<ref>{{Cite news|url=https://www.sciencedaily.com/releases/2012/03/120318143936.htm|title=Physicists simulate strongly correlated fermions|work=ScienceDaily|access-date=October 7, 2018|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Van Houcke|first1=K.|last2=Werner|first2=F.|last3=Kozik|first3=E.|last4=Prokof'ev|first4=N.|last5=Svistunov|first5=B.|last6=Ku|first6=M. J. H.|last7=Sommer|first7=A. T.|last8=Cheuk|first8=L. W.|last9=Schirotzek|first9=A.|date=March 18, 2012|title=Feynman diagrams versus Fermi-gas Feynman emulator|journal=Nature Physics|language=En|volume=8|issue=5|pages=366–370|doi=10.1038/nphys2273|issn=1745-2473|arxiv=1110.3747|bibcode=2012NatPh...8..366V|s2cid=53412117}}</ref>  He is elected Fellow of the American Physical Society for his highly influential works in superfluidity and supersolidity.<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://scholar.google.com/citations?user=wA8fhDcAAAAJ&hl=en|title=Boris Svistunov - Google Scholar Citations|website=scholar.google.com|access-date=September 27, 2018}}</ref>

His research was recognised by his election as Fellow of the American Physical Society.  The citation associated with of his Fellow election in the [[American Physical Society]],<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=&year=&unit_id=&institution=|title=APS Fellow Archive|website=aps.org|language=en|access-date=April 20, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=&year=2008&unit_id=&institution=|title=APS Fellows 2008|website=aps.org|language=en|access-date=April 20, 2017}}</ref> for "pioneering contributions to the theory and practice of Monte Carlo simulations for strongly correlated quantum and classical systems, the invention of the worm algorithm and diagrammatic Monte Carlo techniques, and fundamental theoretical results on superfluid phenomena in quantum gases, liquids, and solids."

He is Outstanding Referee for American Physical Society and Distinguished Referee for Europhysics letters.

He co-authored the book on modern theory of Superfluidity<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.crcpress.com/Superfluid-States-of-Matter/Svistunov-Babaev-Prokofev/p/book/9781439802755|title=Superfluid States of Matter|date=April 15, 2015|website=CRC Press|language=en|access-date=September 27, 2018}}</ref>
